newsitem.title: UK: UK insurance firms hail govt's long term care bill.
newsitem.headline: UK insurance firms hail govt's long term care bill.

text.p: British insurance companies welcomed on Monday government's plans plans to offer private insurance for residential care for the elderly.

"These proposals, if implemented, would ensure that more individuals are able to afford long-term care (LTC) insurance and end the uncertainty about the funding of LTC costs," said Sandy Johnstone, the LTC development manager at insurance giant Commercial Union.
British health secretary Stephen Dorrell unveiled plans to offer private insurance as part of moves to revamp its social services.
The new scheme offers a partnership insurance scheme.
For every pound the insurance scheme pays out, people would be able to keep 1.50 pounds more of their capital than the current means test allows.
Tony Solomon, the LTC expert at Eagle Star, a unit B.A.T Industries, said the government's partnership would encourage more people to make financial arrangements for their own long term care.
Currently, Britons needing long-term care have had to use their own funds until their assets fall to 16,000 pounds, at which point the state would step in to help them.
